name: FortiGate Administrative GUI Connection Refused
checks: Confirm the ingress interface has HTTPS/HTTP administrative access enabled as intended AND confirm the configured admin HTTP/HTTPS port is the port being used. Evidence: `show system interface <interface>`, `show full system global | grep admin-port`, and `show full system global | grep admin-sport`.

Inspect the GUI server certificate before restarting processes. Evidence: `show full system global | grep admin-server-cert`. If the configured certificate is missing, invalid, incompatible, or suspected after an upgrade, Fortinet documents temporarily restoring the built-in certificate with `config system global`, `set admin-server-cert "Fortinet_Factory"`, `end`.

If certificate configuration is valid, confirm the FortiOS GUI service has a listening socket/process. Evidence: `diagnose sys tcpsock | grep httpsd` or the configured port, plus `diagnose sys process pidof httpsd`. On FortiOS versions where admin login handling uses http_authd, use version-appropriate process/debug commands.

Capture one browser attempt and inspect the local response before changing unrelated configuration. Evidence: `diagnose sniffer packet any 'host <client-ip> and port <admin-port>' 4 0 l`, then check crash logs/debug output, local-in restrictions, VIP/port conflicts, and firmware-specific GUI defects only as supported by the capture.
stop_condition: Stop as soon as interface/port, certificate, or GUI listener evidence identifies the cause. Do not revisit a check Python has already marked passed.
resolution: Correct only the isolated administrative-access fault. For a bad GUI certificate, restore a valid admin-server-cert such as Fortinet_Factory only when the evidence supports that cause.
validation: Confirm the FortiGate GUI TCP port accepts a connection.
Confirm the login page renders over HTTPS.
Confirm SSH and normal forwarding remain unaffected.
